results.q: What's the plan for the old Military Circle Mall site?
results.answer:
I can't say that for sure, but here's what I found:

I found no adopted City master plan for the site. What I found is demolition, site testing, and a lot of open questions. This comes from a case file Siren last checked on November 14, 2026.

**Ownership and money**
- WHRO reported on September 1, 2026 that the City owns much of the mall footprint. [Council approved the transfer from the Economic Development Authority on July 15, 2025](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-09-01/260901-militarycircle-saunders). Sentara owns the former J.C. Penney building and much of the parking inside the ring road.
- On April 28, 2026, Council [appropriated up to $600,000 for the mall's operating costs](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5770) (Ordinance No. 50345).
- On August 25, 2026, Council [approved a $200,000 advance to the Economic Development Authority](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949) for site readiness studies (Ordinance No. 50487). The City's letter calls the studies a prerequisite for applying to the state's Business Ready Sites Program for infrastructure money.
- The [cooperation agreement](https\://NorfolkCityVA.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=25519) says the Authority was awarded a $337,750 state grant. The Authority repays the City's advance from that grant.
- The agreement lists the studies: environmental, geotechnical, survey, wetland, traffic, and a preliminary engineering report on water, sewer and transportation. I found no copy of the reports yet.

**Demolition**
- WHRO reported that the 2023 demolition budget was $10 million. WTKR reported on September 29, 2026 that [demolition was priced at nearly $3 million](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/norfolk-leaders-share-updates-on-casino-macarthur-mall-military-circle-mall-and-east-street-garage), with the first phase to start the next month.
- WTKR reported on September 4 that demolition [was expected to take about 15 months](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/military-circle-demolition-moving-forward-in-norfolk-work-begins-in-october).
- I found no City record yet that demolition has begun.

**What comes after**
- As of September 2026, WHRO reported the Deputy City Manager saying the City had no specific master plan. He expected one within about a year, once the studies finish, and hoped incremental development with Sentara could start within three years.
- WHRO reported the studies would take six to eight months, with results likely by spring 2027.
- Redevelopment may happen in phases because of the mixed ownership, per [WTKR on September 4](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/military-circle-demolition-moving-forward-in-norfolk-work-begins-in-october).
- The City's 2017 [vision plan](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/27580/Military_Circle_UDA_Vision_Plan) (adopted January 24, 2017) describes a long-term goal of a high-density, mixed-use neighborhood.

**Open problems**
- [WAVY reported on June 4, 2026](https\://www\.wavy.com/news/norfolk-moving-ahead-with-military-circle-mall-demo-without-ross-ok-citing-public-safety/amp/) that Ross Dress for Less effectively holds a veto inside the ring road. Its lease has extension options through 2036, and it had not consented to demolition.
- WTKR reported on July 14 that breaking the Ross lease would reportedly cost up to $16 million. WHRO reported the City was still negotiating and hoped to resolve it by the end of demolition.
- WHRO said the three 2021 redevelopment proposals were all shelved as financially unworkable by late 2023.
- I found no Military Circle project in the adopted FY 2027–2031 capital plan. The City Manager said the East Side library and recreation center would go to the former Poplar Hall Elementary site, to avoid the Military Circle delays.

What this might add up to: I read the records as showing a City that is clearing and testing the site first and deciding what to build later. The reports due around spring 2027 look like the next marker. The Ross lease and Sentara's share of the land look like the main things that could shape or slow any plan. I'd treat the long-term vision as a goal, not a commitment.

results.q: What does the Military Circle cooperation agreement (Ordinance 50487) say about paying back the advance?
results.answer:
The repayment terms in [Ordinance No. 50487](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949) are short. They tie repayment to the state grant, and the pages I read set no repayment date.

**The advance.** In the [cooperation agreement (Exhibit A)](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=25519), page 1, the Authority expects the site reports to cost $337,750.00. It asked the City to advance $200,000.00 of that. The agreement calls this the "Site Reports Funding Advance."

**Repayment.** The agreement says the City provides the advance on the condition that the Authority repays it "upon receipt of the Grant funds from VBRSP." That is the Virginia Business Ready Sites Program grant. Section 2 (page 1) says the Authority "will reimburse City for the full amount of the Site Reports Funding Advance" once it receives the grant funds. It also says the Authority must work in good faith to finish the reports on time so the grant reimburses it.

**What I found no text on.** On pages 1–3 I found no repayment deadline, no interest, and no instructions for the case where the grant isn't awarded or paid. Section 12 says each party's rights and remedies are cumulative. That is a general clause, not a repayment term. I didn't read page 4, which is probably the signature page.

**The vote.** City Council adopted the ordinance on Aug 25, 2026, with all eight members voting aye ("ADOPTED \[UNANIMOUS]"). The vote record is from draft minutes. The City's cover letter says the work is a prerequisite for applying to a Virginia Business Ready Sites Program site development grant for future infrastructure.

For the exact terms, check the signed agreement with the City Manager's Office or the City Attorney's office.

results.q: How much does Norfolk budget for tree care?
results.answer:
I found no budget line for tree care alone. The closest match is the Parks and Forestry Operations unit, which also covers mowing, landscaping, litter control and athletic fields.

**What I found for Parks and Forestry Operations** (Parks & Recreation, from the City's [Annual Expenditures data](https\://data.norfolk.gov)):
- **FY2025:** budget $11,728,050, actual $11,536,917.
- **FY2026:** budget $12,661,811, actual $12,169,859.
- **FY2027:** budget $13,139,514. Only about 38.9% of the year had passed on 2026-11-20, and $4,562,793 had been spent so far.

The FY2027 and FY2026 figures include department-wide changes. The FY2027 Parks and Recreation section says the bureau manages street trees, trees on public property, open space and the city nursery. Its staffing table lists 2 Tree Trimmer I and 3 Tree Trimmer II positions.

**Tree-specific items in the budget books:**
- **FY2024:** a [$250,000 adjustment](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/78214/10-Department-Budgets) for the tree care maintenance contract, which the book says is used to remove decaying or diseased trees. A Forestry Supervisor ($119,572) was requested but not funded.
- **FY2025:** [$400,000 added](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/88686/08-Department-Budgets) for tree maintenance to reduce a backlog the budget attributes to the pandemic.

These two items come from a verified case file on Norfolk's trees, which cites those budget books. I did not read the pages themselves.

**Context from that case file:**
- The FY2024 budget book reported fulfilling 5% of street-tree pruning requests in FY2021 and 9% in FY2022. It projected 5% for FY2023.
- A draft City Auditor report from April 2023 says Forestry has been unable to adopt a proactive maintenance program.
- The case file says the pruning-fulfillment measure is absent from the FY2025 and FY2026 books. It says the FY2027 book replaces it with trees planted. That has not been re-checked by a second reader.

For an exact tree-only figure, you could request the tree-care contracts and invoices, plus a Forestry work-order export, from the City under Virginia FOIA.

I can also read the FY2027 Parks and Recreation budget actions in full if you'd like.

- **Costs:** The completed removals show total costs from $0.00 to $585.55. The Graydon removal shows $0.00.

The dataset assigns each work order to one civic league, based on its primary street. A job near a boundary may be counted in a neighboring league. These are work orders, not a count of trees. I didn't check whether replacements were planted.

results.q: What does the zoning ordinance say about short-term rentals in residential districts?
results.answer:
I found the short-term rental rules in three places in the [Zoning Ordinance](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance). The City's PDF cover says it was updated October 13, 2026. Amendments after that date aren't in my copy.

**Use table (§3.2.12, p. 198–204)**
- In the [residential districts use table](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=198), the row for "Short-term rental unit (vacation rental)" shows P/C in some districts and C in others.
- The table lists seven entries across nine district columns, and the extracted text drops the blank cells. I can't tell which district gets which entry. Check the PDF table for your district. A Zoning Determination from City Planning is the binding answer.
- A separate accessory-use row, "Short-term rental unit (homestay)", shows P/C in all nine residential columns.

**Performance standards (§4.2.3, "Short-term rental unit (vacation rental)", around p. 507)**
- **Definition:** The ordinance defines it as renting a dwelling, or part of one, to a single-party guest for one night to fewer than 30 consecutive nights, "when all owners of the dwelling have their primary residence elsewhere."
- **When a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is required:**
  - The use isn't registered.
  - In R-C, SF-2, SF-4 or SF-6, the property lacks the required off-street parking or has four or more bedrooms.
  - In R-C or D, the unit is in a building with three or more dwelling units.
- **Multifamily CUPs:** The application must ask that all units in the building be available as rentals. It must also show that tenants were notified.
- **Before renting:** The operator needs a Zoning Certificate and a business license. A zoning certificate lasts at most two years, or up to ten years if a CUP sets a longer term.
- **Size limits:** Each zoning lot is limited to 24 units in R-C and 9 units in any other district. Occupancy is two guests per bedroom, with no more than 10 guests in five bedrooms. Properties with more than 9 units need on-site management.
- **Operating rules:**
  - Bookings must go through online platforms.
  - A contact sign is required, and the contact must be able to be on site within 20 minutes.
  - Remote entry is required, with the access code changed between stays.
  - Cameras must face the parking area and exterior common areas.
  - Interior decibel meters are required.
  - Waste bins must be put away within 24 hours of collection.
  - Condo and co-op units need written permission from the association or board.
- **Optional registration:** A registration lasts two years. It requires:
  - an emergency contact
  - proof of a fire inspection
  - agreement to law-enforcement entry for inspection
  - guest records
  - at least $300,000 in premises liability insurance
  - stated bedroom and guest maximums
  - the additional parking required
- **Penalties for registered units:** The first violation brings a warning, with 14 days to fix it. The second within two years brings a four-month suspension from the registry. The third brings removal and one year of ineligibility.

**Short-Term Rental Limitation Overlay (§3.9.22, p. 439–441)**
- The [overlay](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439) adds standards where it applies, and its provisions govern if they conflict with the base district. Its stated purpose is to reduce the effects of "proliferation" of rentals in a concentrated residential area.
- Two kinds of property can register under it:
  - Any property with an active zoning approval (a CUP or Zoning Certificate) as of June 1, 2026. An approval that expired no more than 60 days before a new application also counts.
  - Any single-family or two-family property more than 300 linear feet from a rental with an active approval.
- A CUP is required if the property meets the location test but lacks the minimum off-street parking.
- For registered units, the third violation in two years brings a certified-mail notice. The fourth removes the property from the registry for two years.
- For CUP units, the zoning administrator may recommend that City Council revoke the permit after the fourth violation. A revoked property may be ineligible for two years.
- I didn't check which parcels sit inside the overlay. I can look up an address if you give me one.

**What I didn't read**
- I didn't read the parking table (Table 5.1.7(D)) that sets the required spaces.
- I didn't read the homestay standards (§4.3.3).
- The City Code isn't in my tools. Chapter 22 is referenced in the ordinance, but I didn't read it.

For a binding answer on one property, a landowner, resident or business owner can request a written interpretation from the Zoning Administrator (§2.3.8).

results.q: What's the plan for the old Military Circle Mall site?
results.answer:
I can't say that for sure, but here's what I found. A Siren case file, checked against City records and news reports as of November 14, 2026, shows money and studies moving ahead while the reuse plan itself is not yet set.

**Ownership and leases**
- WHRO reported on September 1, 2026 that the City owns much of the mall footprint, but Sentara owns the former J.C. Penney building and much of the parking inside the ring road. ([WHRO](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-09-01/260901-militarycircle-saunders))
- Council approved the transfer of the site from the Economic Development Authority on July 15, 2025. In October 2025, Council approved the City taking on the mall's leases and its 1968 operating agreement from the Authority. The case file reports the October 2025 vote; I did not pull that record myself.

**Money approved so far**
- On April 28, 2026, Council appropriated up to $600,000, transferred from the Authority, for the mall's operating expenses. ([Ordinance No. 50345](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5770))
- On August 25, 2026, Council approved a $200,000 City advance to the Authority for site readiness work. The Authority has been awarded a $337,750 state site characterization grant, which is meant to repay the advance. The City's letter calls these studies a prerequisite for applying to the state's Business Ready Sites Program. ([Ordinance No. 50487](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949))
- The agreement lists the studies to be done: a site certification report, geotechnical, survey, environmental, cultural resource, species, wetland and traffic studies, and a preliminary engineering report on water, sewer and transportation. I found no copy of those reports in this review. ([Ordinance No. 50487, Exhibit A](https\://NorfolkCityVA.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=25519))

**Demolition**
- WHRO reported on September 1, 2026 that the City aimed to start demolition in October. The Deputy City Manager said the 2023 demolition budget was $10 million and would not grow. ([WHRO](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-09-01/260901-militarycircle-saunders))
- WTKR reported on September 29, 2026 that demolition was priced at nearly $3 million, with the first phase to start the next month. ([WTKR](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/norfolk-leaders-share-updates-on-casino-macarthur-mall-military-circle-mall-and-east-street-garage))
- WTKR reported on July 14, 2026 that 13 bids had been submitted, and that breaking the Ross Dress for Less lease could reportedly cost up to $16 million. ([WTKR](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/multiple-bids-submitted-for-military-circle-demo-project-city-leader-reports))
- WAVY reported on June 4, 2026 that Ross had not consented to the demolition as the City put it out to bid, and that Ross effectively holds a veto inside the ring road. ([WAVY](https\://www\.wavy.com/news/norfolk-moving-ahead-with-military-circle-mall-demo-without-ross-ok-citing-public-safety/amp/))
- I found no City record yet that demolition has begun.

**Timeline and what comes after**
- WHRO reported that the site studies would take six to eight months, with results likely by spring 2027. The Deputy City Manager expected a master plan about a year after the studies end, and hoped incremental development with Sentara could start within three years. ([WHRO](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-09-01/260901-militarycircle-saunders))
- WTKR reported on September 4, 2026 that demolition was expected to take about 15 months. ([WTKR](https\://www\.wtkr.com/news/in-the-community/norfolk/military-circle-demolition-moving-forward-in-norfolk-work-begins-in-october))
- The 2017 vision plan for the area describes a long-term goal of a fully redeveloped, high-density mixed-use neighborhood. The case file cites this plan; I did not open it.

**Not settled**
- As of September 2026, the Deputy City Manager told WHRO the City had no specific master plan for the site.
- The Ross lease was still being negotiated as of September 2026.
- The adopted FY 2027–2031 capital plan names no Military Circle project. It funds $1,000,000 to design an East Side library and recreation center at the former Poplar Hall Elementary site instead. ([Capital Improvement Plan](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/113999/14-Capital-Improvement-Plan)) The City Manager told WHRO on May 20, 2026 that Poplar Hall was chosen to avoid delays tied to the Military Circle site. ([WHRO](https\://www\.whro.org/local-government/2026-05-20/052026-cipapproved-saunders))

What this might add up to: The City has spent on the site, approved about $800,000 in City-side money so far, and is trying to get the land studied before deciding what goes there. The records show the demolition timing depends on the Ross lease and the bid, and the reuse plan depends on the studies, which are not due until about spring 2027. The Sentara parcels and the Ross lease are the open questions that the records do not yet resolve.

**The definition (§4.2.3, page 507)**
A short-term rental unit is a dwelling, or part of one, rented to a single party for at least one night and fewer than 30 consecutive nights. The table lists the short-term rental unit with "P" (permitted) and "C" (CUP) entries across the residential districts. The column headings did not come through with the entries, so I cannot say which districts allow it by right and which need a CUP.

**The Short-Term Rental Limitation Overlay (§3.9.22, [page 439](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439))**
- Its stated purpose is to reduce the effects of many short-term rentals concentrated in a residential area.
- Where it conflicts with the base district rules, the overlay governs.
- Registration eligibility covers properties with an active CUP or Zoning Certificate for a short-term rental as of June 1, 2026. A recently expired approval counts if it expired no more than 60 days before a new application. Single-family and two-family homes more than 300 linear feet from an active short-term rental are also eligible.
- A property that does not meet all minimum off-street parking requirements may operate only with a CUP.

**Penalties in the overlay (§3.9.22, page 440)**
- For registered rentals, the third violation in two years brings notice by certified mail. The fourth violation removes the property from the registry for two years.
- For CUP rentals, the third violation brings notice that the next one may lead to a recommendation for revocation. The fourth may lead the Zoning Administrator to recommend revocation to City Council.

results.q: What's the plan for the old Military Circle Mall site?
results.answer:
I can't say that for sure, but here's what I found:

**Short answer: I found no settled end-use plan yet. What the records show is ownership, money for studies, and a planned demolition. I found no master plan in the records I can reach.**

**What the City has done**
- Council approved the transfer of the mall property from the Economic Development Authority on July 15, 2025, in [Ordinance No. 50067](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949)'s companion record ([agenda item 5374](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949)). WHRO reported on September 1, 2026 that the City owns much of the footprint, but Sentara owns the former J.C. Penney building and much of the parking inside the ring road.
- On April 28, 2026, Council appropriated up to $600,000 from the Authority for the mall's operating costs ([Ordinance No. 50345](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5770)).
- On August 25, 2026, Council approved a $200,000 advance to the Authority for site readiness testing ([Ordinance No. 50487](https\://norfolkcityva.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=5949)). The agreement says the Authority has been awarded a $337,750 state grant, and the advance is to be repaid from it.

**The studies**
The agreement lists the work: a site certification report, geotechnical, survey, environmental (Phase I and II), cultural resource, species, wetland and traffic studies, and a preliminary engineering report on water, sewer and transportation. WHRO reported on September 1, 2026 that the reports were expected to take six to eight months, with results likely by spring 2027. I found no copy of these reports in the records.

**Demolition**
- WHRO reported on September 1, 2026 that the City aimed to start demolition in October.
- WTKR reported on September 29, 2026 that demolition was priced at nearly $3 million, with the first phase to begin the next month. WTKR reported on September 4 that the work was expected to take about 15 months.
- WHRO reported that the Deputy City Manager said the $10 million budget approved in 2023 would not grow.
- I found no City record that demolition has begun.

**Ross Dress for Less**
- WAVY reported on June 4, 2026 that Ross effectively holds a veto inside the ring road, and that the City put the demolition out to bid without Ross's consent.
- WTKR reported on July 14, 2026 that breaking the Ross lease would reportedly cost up to $16 million.
- As of September 2026, WHRO reported the City was still negotiating the Ross lease.

**The longer-term plan**
- WHRO reported that the Deputy City Manager expected a master plan about a year after the studies conclude, and hoped incremental development with Sentara could start within three years.
- The [adopted FY 2027–2031 capital plan](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/113999/14-Capital-Improvement-Plan) names no Military Circle project. It funds $1,000,000 to design an East Side library and recreation center at the former Poplar Hall Elementary site.
- WHRO reported on May 20, 2026 that the City Manager said the Poplar Hall site was chosen to avoid delays tied to Military Circle.
- The [2017 vision plan](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/27580/Military_Circle_UDA_Vision_Plan) describes a long-term goal of a completely redeveloped, high-density mixed-use neighborhood. WHRO reported that three 2021 redevelopment proposals were shelved as financially unworkable by late 2023.

The case file I used reflects records through November 14, 2026. My check of agenda titles found no newer mall items after the August 25 action.

What this might add up to: The City now owns most of the site and is paying for the studies and demolition, but I found no record showing what the land will become. The studies that would inform a master plan are due around spring 2027, and the Ross lease and Sentara's ownership are still open. The plan appears to be at the testing and demolition stage, not a development plan. I found no record of who decided the demolition timeline beyond the Council actions above. For that, the City Manager's office or your Council representative would know.

I have asked for the site readiness reports to be added as a source, so you can request them.

results.q: How much does Norfolk budget for tree care?
results.answer:
I found no separate budget line for tree care. The closest figure I found is the budget for the Park and Forestry Operations unit in Parks and Recreation. That unit covers more than trees. The FY2027 budget book describes it as managing the urban canopy, including street trees, and also as maintaining grounds for parks, public buildings, medians, schools and athletic fields.

Figures for that whole unit, from the City's expenditure records (updated 2026-11-20):

- **FY2027 (adopted plan):** $13,139,514. FY2027 is still in progress, about 38.9% elapsed on November 20, with $4,562,793 spent so far.
- **FY2026:** budget $12,661,811; actual spending $12,169,859 (96.1% of budget).
- **FY2025:** budget $11,728,050; actual spending $11,536,917 (98.4% of budget).

The expenditure data shows the budget figures after mid-year transfers and amendments for FY2025 and FY2026. The FY2027 figure is the adopted plan.

Tree-specific amounts appear in the adopted budgets, as the City's tree findings record them:

- **FY2024:** a $250,000 adjustment for a tree care maintenance contract, which the City says removes decaying or diseased trees ([FY2024 Adopted Budget](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/78214/10-Department-Budgets)).
- **FY2025:** $400,000 added for tree maintenance to reduce a backlog the City attributes to the pandemic ([FY2025 Adopted Budget](https\://www\.norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/88686/08-Department-Budgets)).

I did not check whether these amounts appear in the expenditure data.

On the backlog, the FY2024 budget book reported fulfilling 5% of street-tree pruning requests in FY2021 and 9% in FY2022, and projected 5% for FY2023. A draft City Auditor report says Forestry has been unable to adopt a proactive maintenance program. The findings record notes that the pruning measure is absent from the FY2025 and FY2026 books, and that this has not yet been re-checked.

results.q: What does the zoning ordinance say about short-term rentals in residential districts?
results.answer:
I can't say that for sure, but here's what I found:

- **Use table:** The residential district use table lists "Short-term rental unit (vacation rental)" with permitted (P) or conditional (C) marks, and points to §4.2.3.F(10)(e) for its standards. The excerpt I could read did not show which mark applies to which residential district. See §3.2.12, page 201.
- **Definition:** §4.2.3 defines a short-term rental as a dwelling rented to a single party for at least one night and fewer than 30 consecutive nights, where all owners have their primary residence elsewhere. It says a Conditional Use Permit is required when the unit is not registered under §4.2.3.F(10)(f), and lists districts where a CUP is also required. The excerpt cut off before the full district list. See §4.2.3, page 507.
- **Overlay (§3.9.22, Short-Term Rental Limitation Overlay):** The overlay's stated purpose is to reduce the effects of many short-term rentals in a concentrated residential area. Where it conflicts with the base zoning, the overlay governs. Within the overlay:
  - Properties with an active zoning approval (a CUP or Zoning Certificate for a short-term rental) as of June 1, 2026 can register to continue.
  - Single-family and two-family properties more than 300 linear feet from an active short-term rental can also register.
  - A property without the minimum off-street parking can operate only with a CUP.
  - For registered units, a third violation in two years brings a certified-mail notice, and a fourth removes the property from the registry for two years.
  - For CUP units, a third violation brings notice that the next may lead to a recommendation to City Council for revocation, and a fourth may lead to that recommendation.

  See [§3.9.22, page 439](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance#page=439).
- **Home-stays:** §2.3.6 exempts a registered home-stay dwelling from the administrative review steps in that section. See §2.3.6, page 86.

I did not find the full text of §4.2.3.F(10)(e) and (f), which holds the registration requirements and the full district list. I also did not check whether any particular parcel sits inside the STRL-O overlay. These texts are current through the October 13, 2026 update shown on the PDF's cover.

What this might add up to: the ordinance appears to allow short-term rentals in residential districts either by right or with a CUP, depending on the district. Inside the overlay, the City appears to have tied continued use to registration, a June 1, 2026 cutoff for existing approvals, and escalating penalties. Whether a specific home qualifies depends on the full registration text and its location, which I did not confirm.

For a specific address, a parcel lookup would show whether it falls in the overlay. The binding answer for a particular property is a Zoning Determination from City Planning. The full PDF is at the [Zoning Ordinance link](https\://norfolk.gov/DocumentCenter/View/35581/Adopted-Zoning-Ordinance), and the contacts below can point you to the zoning staff.
